source_text: Quis dominus caeli inuocabitur, qui non prius factor ostenditur? gratias enim, inquit, ago et confiteor, domine caeli, quod ea, quae erant abscondita sapientibus et prudentibus, reuelaueris paruulis. quae ista? et cuius? et a quo abscondita? et a quo reuelata? si a deo Marcionis abscondita et reuelata, qui omnino nihil praemiserat, in quo aliquid absconditum esse potuisset, non prophetias, non parabolas, non uisiones, non ulla rerum aut uerborum aut nominum argumenta per allegorias et figuras uel aenigmatum nebulas obumbrata? sed 'ipsam magnitudinem sui absconderat, quam cum maxime per Christum reuelabat'. satis inique. quid enim deliquerant sapientes et prudentes, ut absconderetur illis deus, ad quem cognoscendum non suffecerat sapientia atque prudentia illorum, nulla uia data ab ipso per aliquam operum praedicationem uel uestigia, per quae sapientes atque prudentes . deducerentur? quamquam et si in aliquo deliquissent erga deum ignotum pone, nunc notum, non tamen zeloten eum experiri debuissent, qui dissimilis creatoris inducitur. igitur si nec materias praemiserat, in quibus aliquid occultasset, nec reos habuerat, a quibus occultasset, nec debuerat occultasse, etiam si habuisset, iam nec reuelator ipse erit, qui absconditor non fuit, — ita nec dominus caeli nec pater Christi — sed ille, in quem competunt omnia. nam et abscondit praemisso obscuritatis propheticae instrumento, cuius intellectum fides mereretur — nisi enim credideritis, non intellegetis — et reos habuit sapientes atque prudentes ex ipsis' operibus tot ac tantis intellegibilem deum non requirentes uel perperam in illum philosophantes et ingenia haereticis sumministrantes, et nouissime zelotes est. denique olim hoc per Esaiam contionabatur, quod Christus gratulatur: perdam sapientiam sapientium et prudentiam prudentium celabo, sicut et alibi tam abscondisse (se) quam reuelaturum esse significat:
pass_a_gloss: Who will be called Lord of heaven, who is not first shown to be the Creator? For he says, I give thanks and I confess, Lord of heaven, that you have revealed to little ones the things that were hidden from the wise and the prudent. What things are these? And whose? And from whom were they hidden? And from whom were they revealed? If they were hidden and revealed by the God of Marcion, who had not sent anything beforehand, in which something could have been hidden, not prophecies, not parables, not visions, not any arguments of things or words or names through allegories and figures or clouds of enigmas? But he had hidden his own greatness, which he was revealing especially through Christ. This is quite unjust. For what had the wise and the prudent done wrong, that God should be hidden from them, to know whom their wisdom and prudence had not been sufficient, no way having been given by him through any works or preaching or footprints, through which the wise and the prudent might have been led? Although even if they had done wrong in some way towards the unknown God, now known, they should not have had to experience a zealot, who is introduced as unlike the Creator. Therefore, if he had not sent beforehand the materials in which he could have hidden something, and he had not had those from whom he could have hidden, and he should not have hidden even if he had had them, then he will not even be the revealer, who was not the hider, — so neither the Lord of heaven nor the Father of Christ — but the one to whom all things belong. For he also hides, having sent beforehand the instrument of prophetic obscurity, whose understanding faith deserves — for unless you believe, you will not understand — and he had the wise and the prudent as guilty, not seeking the intelligible God from his so many and great works, or philosophizing wrongly about him, and providing minds for heretics, and finally he is a zealot. Lastly, he once proclaimed this through Isaiah, which Christ welcomes: I will destroy the wisdom of the wise and I will hide the prudence of the prudent, just as he also signifies elsewhere that he has hidden and will reveal himself:

pass_b_english: What kind of Lord of heaven are we talking about if he's not first shown to be the Creator? The Lord of heaven says he's grateful that the things hidden from the wise and the prudent have been revealed to little ones (Matthew 11:25). But what exactly are these things, and who do they belong to? Who hid them, and who revealed them? If it was the God of Marcion who hid and revealed them, then we have a problem - this God didn't send any prophecies, parables, or visions beforehand, so there was nothing to hide. The God of Marcion just hid his own greatness, which he's now revealing through Christ. That's not fair. What did the wise and the prudent do to deserve being kept in the dark about God? Their wisdom and prudence weren't enough to know God, but that's because God didn't give them any way to know him - no signs, no preaching, no clues to follow. Even if they had done something wrong, they shouldn't have to deal with a zealot God who's unlike the Creator. If God didn't send any signs beforehand and didn't have anyone to hide things from, then he's not really the one revealing things now - and that means he's not the Lord of heaven or the Father of Christ. It's the one who has everything under his control who's really in charge. This God hides and reveals, using prophetic language that's hard to understand - you need faith to get it (Isaiah 6:9-10). The wise and the prudent are guilty of not seeking God despite all the evidence, and they've even helped heretics with their wrong ideas. And in the end, this God is a zealot. As he said through Isaiah, he'll destroy the wisdom of the wise and hide the prudence of the prudent (Isaiah 29:14), and he's also said that he's hidden himself and will reveal himself (Matthew 11:27).

review.notes: Pass B adds several scripture citations that are not present in the Locked Latin source, which is a violation of the rule against adding to the text. Specifically, Pass B adds '(Matthew 11:25)', '(Isaiah 6:9-10)', '(Isaiah 29:14)', and '(Matthew 11:27)'. While these may be contextually accurate to the underlying biblical allusions, they are not in the provided Latin text. Furthermore, Pass B's translation of 'in quem competunt omnia' as 'It's the one who has everything under his control who's really in charge' is a significant departure from the literal sense 'but he [the one to whom all things belong/are due]'.

reasons: Pass A omits the clause 'qui non prius factor ostenditur' ('who is not first shown to be the Creator') and instead translates it as 'if he's not first shown to be the Creator', which is a paraphrase and not a direct translation of the Latin.

Pass B incorrectly cites Isaiah 29:14 for the quote 'I will destroy the wisdom of the wise and I will hide the prudence of the prudent' when the Latin text explicitly says 'per Esaiam' ('through Isaiah'), and the actual source is Isaiah 29:14, not Matthew 11:25 as cited in the English translation.
